classification.difficultyReason: Select the exposed hemisphere surfaces, then rearrange the area formula to find the radius.

content.prompt: A hemispherical tent is made using $28\text{ m}^2$ of material. Find, correct to two decimal places, the radius of the tent if:

spec.description: Upright hemispherical tent with a semicircular dome silhouette, elliptical circular base, dashed rear base arc and marked base centre. No measurements or radius labels are supplied.
spec.mathematics: Hemisphere with a circular base; the presence of a material floor is varied in the parts.
spec.answerVisibility: No answers or inferred measurements are shown.

children.label: a
children.prompt: the tent does not have a material floor

answer.short:
$2.11\text{ m}$

Use only the curved surface area, $2\pi r^2$.
answer.worked:
Without a floor, the material covers half the surface of a sphere.

$\begin{align*}2\pi r^2&=28\\r^2&=\frac{28}{2\pi}\\r&=\sqrt{\frac{14}{\pi}}\text{ m}\\r&\approx2.11\text{ m}\end{align*}$

children.label: b
children.prompt: the tent does have a material floor

answer.short:
$1.72\text{ m}$

Include the circular floor: $2\pi r^2+\pi r^2=3\pi r^2$.
answer.worked:
Include both the curved surface and the circular floor.

$\begin{align*}2\pi r^2+\pi r^2&=28\\3\pi r^2&=28\\r^2&=\frac{28}{3\pi}\\r&=\sqrt{\frac{28}{3\pi}}\text{ m}\\r&\approx1.72\text{ m}\end{align*}$
